summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all four paragraphs of the selected Greek working source. Both preserve the three forms, the aging comparison, both causes of weakness, exclusive expectation of sleep, self-surrender to negligence, the negative casting-of-anxieties clause, the shattered mind and sorrow-induced aging, and the universal chair/support explanation with its purpose clause. The question and reply remain distinct, as do Lord and sir. The simplified sentence divisions do not introduce a concrete fidelity defect. The notes accurately disclose the supplied reports’ variant readings, corrections, gaps, bracketed material, and mediated Ethiopic rendering without replacing the selected working readings or presenting editorial additions as intact first-hand text. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied source and disclosure evidence; it does not authenticate unseen images, independently verify the cited editions, or certify exhaustive collation.
